newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed, feeders down sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed, feeders down sharply.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed with nearby contracts up and deferreds lower after USDA's Cattle-on-Feed report. Feeder cattle finished sharply lower with the bulk of the pressure coming from higher corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle closed up 0.425 cent per lb to off 0.350 cent with April up 0.125 at 66.575 cents. Feeder cattle were down 1.225 to 0.200 with March off most at 66.725 cents.

Friday's USDA data showed more than expected cattle were placed on feed in January which pressured deferred months, traders said. USDA said 25 percent more cattle were placed on feed in January in the seven key states than a year ago, well above the average of analysts' estimates at 107.5 percent.
But the number of cattle marketed in January, at 107 percent, exceeded the 101.3 average estimate and lent support to nearby live cattle futures Tuesday, sources said.

"Most people think that what (USDA) did with the placements this time is kind of a combination of what they should have done in December and January -- December (placements) looks way understated," said Karen Curry, livestock analyst with Rosenthal Collins.
Bull spreading was evident on the report.
Many of the cattle put on feed recently were light weight and it will take longer than usual before they are ready for market, traders said.
Nearbys also found support on talk that packers look short of slaughter-ready cattle. Wholesale beef prices are starting to firm and they will want to have more cattle around them, traders added.

R.J. O'Brien, LFG and E.D.&F. Man bought February while scattered buying in April offset selling by Cargill Investor Services, Prudential Securities and E.D.&F. Man, traders said. In live cattle options, commission houses bought April 66 to 70 calls and locals sold August 62 puts and 66 and 68 calls. Volatility in April was steady-weak and down in August.

A sharp advance in corn futures added to weakness from deferred live cattle futures to pressure feeders. Technical sell stops were touched off on the setback and March fell to its lowest level since December 26. The market looks technically very weak, they said.

Funds liquidated on the break with Dean Witter, ADM Investor Services and LIT division of First Options notable sellers. Cargill spread long August feeders/short December live cattle and E.D.&F. Man spread long August feeders/short May feeders, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.02 at $68.98 per cwt.
